around.headline: Father allegedly stabs daughter over Rs 40 lakh 'reverse dowry' and salary demand
around.summary: Police arrested a 52-year-old auto driver for allegedly stabbing his daughter, an assistant professor, in her college chamber after she and her mother refused his demand that her prospective in-laws pay him Rs 40 lakh and that she keep handing over her monthly salary to him even after marriage; she is hospitalised. The Dowry Prohibition Act covers demands like this even before any money changes hands — you don't need to wait for it to turn violent to file a complaint.

around.headline: 10-year-old girl killed by speeding car while crossing road to school near Nelamangala
around.summary: A schoolgirl was killed by a speeding car while crossing the road on her way to school near Nelamangala. If your child's route to school lacks a marked crossing, speed breaker, or signage, flag it to BBMP or the traffic police rather than waiting for another accident.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Service road closure triggers major traffic chaos on the Outer Ring Road
around.summary: A service road closure on the ORR has caused significant congestion for commuters on that stretch. Check live traffic conditions before you set out this morning and keep a backup route in mind for peak hours.

around.headline: Metro overcrowding relief in sight as BMRCL clears another hurdle for new trains
around.summary: BMRCL has cleared another regulatory step for new Distance-To-Go (DTG) six-coach trainsets on the Green Line, meant to ease peak-hour overcrowding; the new trains are expected in service around August. Relief isn't immediate, but more capacity is coming for regular commuters on that line.

around.headline: SIR nears completion: over 34 lakh Bengaluru electors flagged ASDDO, some say forms never arrived
around.summary: As Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls enters its final phase, more than 34 lakh Bengaluru electors (nearly half the state's total) have been classified as Absent, Shifted, Deceased, Duplicate or Others — while some residents in Bengaluru and Kodagu say enumeration forms never reached them despite claims of 100% distribution. Check your own entry on the CEO Karnataka site or Voter Helpline app before the final list is published, so you're not wrongly dropped.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald, The Hindu

around.headline: Trump administration weighs $100,000 fee for international students to work in the US after graduating
around.summary: The US administration is reportedly considering a $100,000 fee tied to Optional Practical Training (OPT), the visa extension that lets international graduates work in the US after their studies; it isn't finalised or law yet. If you or your family are budgeting for a US postgrad degree with an eye on working there afterward, factor in this uncertainty before committing funds.

street_smart.title: Your father keeps pressuring you to promise your future in-laws will pay him money directly, and to keep handing over your own salary to him even after you're married — he's getting angrier every time you and your mother push back. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real case reported today: a 52-year-old Bengaluru auto driver allegedly stabbed his daughter, an assistant professor, in her college chamber after she and her mother refused his demand that the groom's family pay him Rs 40 lakh and that she keep giving him her monthly salary after marriage (Deccan Herald, News Karnataka, Siasat).
street_smart.situation: A family member has been demanding money and ongoing financial control from you — not a stranger, not a scammer, someone you live with or answer to — and the pressure has been building for a while with arguments but no outside record of it. You have to decide how to respond before things escalate further.

choices.text: Write down the dates and details of each demand and confrontation, tell at least one person outside the situation (another relative, a friend, your workplace or college), and file a complaint or approach the local police/Women's Helpline (181) about the pattern before it turns physical.
choices.feedback: Correct. A dated, written record and at least one outside witness are exactly what turn a private family dispute into something police or courts can act on. You can report coercion or dowry-related demands under the Dowry Prohibition Act and the Domestic Violence Act before any money changes hands or any violence happens — you don't have to wait for 'proof' of harm first.

choices.text: Keep it inside the family and try to privately talk your father out of it yourselves, without telling anyone else or creating any record of what's been demanded.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Coercion that stays entirely private, unwitnessed and unreported tends to escalate rather than resolve — months of arguments over money can build up with no outside awareness and no paper trail, which is exactly the pattern that left this case with no prior complaint on record before it turned violent. Keeping it contained removes the two things that actually create protection: documentation and a second person who knows.

choices.text: Agree to send the money and keep handing over your salary after marriage, since it's 'just money' and might keep the peace.
choices.feedback: Giving in to an escalating demand rarely ends the pattern — it tends to confirm that pressure works, which often invites bigger asks later, and it does nothing to create a record if you do need protection down the line. If you feel you must offer something to de-escalate in the moment, still document it and tell someone — compliance alone isn't a safety plan.

choices.text: Cut off all contact and refuse to meet your father anywhere, without telling police, a protection officer, or anyone else that there's an ongoing risk.
choices.feedback: Going silent without any protective step leaves you exposed if he shows up unannounced — which is exactly what happened here, at the daughter's workplace. The Domestic Violence Act covers adult women facing coercion or abuse from a parent, not just a spouse, and a protection order or police awareness is what backs up a decision to cut contact.

takeaways: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 criminalises demanding or giving dowry in either direction — including a parent demanding money from a daughter's in-laws — and a complaint can be filed before any money changes hands.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers adult women facing abuse or financial coercion from any family member they share a household with, not only a spouse.

If a family member threatens or pressures you over money, write down what was said and when as it happens, and tell at least one person outside the situation — that record is what makes a later complaint or protection order actionable.

quiz.q: In today's Bengaluru news, what made the dowry demand that led to a stabbing at a college campus unusual?
options: The father demanded money from the groom's side and wanted his daughter to keep giving him her salary after marriage
The groom's family demanded gold ornaments from the bride
A husband demanded his wife's inheritance be signed over to him
A landlord demanded a dowry-style deposit from a tenant
quiz.why: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 makes any dowry demand illegal regardless of direction — it isn't limited to a groom's side demanding from a bride's family.

quiz.q: Karnataka's ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls flags certain voters under the category 'ASDDO.' What does the O stand for?
quiz.why: ASDDO stands for Absent, Shifted, Deceased, Duplicate and Others — voters flagged this way need re-verification before the final roll is published.

quiz.q: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing a $100,000 fee tied to which US visa extension used by international graduates?
quiz.why: OPT lets international students work in the US for a period after graduating; almost 300,000 students were on it as of last year, a large share from India.

quiz.q: The Cauvery river, central to a long-running water-sharing dispute involving Bengaluru's home state, originates in which state?
quiz.why: The Cauvery originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu district, Karnataka, before flowing on into Tamil Nadu.

quiz.q: Which greenhouse gas is released in the largest quantity when fossil fuels like petrol and diesel are burned?
quiz.why: CO2 from burning fossil fuels for transport and power generation is the single largest contributor to human-caused greenhouse gas emissions worldwide.
